newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe Catholic bishops urge talks on nurses.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe Catholic bishops urge talks on nurses.

text.p: Zimbabwean Catholic bishops on Saturday urged the government to address the grievances of thousands of nurses it fired this week after they defied an order to end a 10-day strike.

"The profession of doctor or nurse is more than simply a commercial career - it is a dedicated vocation of service to the community and to its members," the Catholic Bishops' Conference said in a statement.
"At the same time, we recognise that doctors and nurses in the public service have for many years received little reward for their labours," it said.
"It may even be that their essential services have been taken for granted. It is essential that their genuine grievances should be treated by government with great seriousness," it added.

Human rights groups and opposition parties have slammed the government for high-handedness after it sacked 11,000 nurses who took to the streets on October 21 to press demands for higher pay, allowances and negotiations on their conditions of service.

On Thursday, the southern African country's main human rights group, Zimrights, warned the government's tough stance would only worsen the crisis gripping public hospitals which have had to recruit army and Red Cross personnel to help doctors who are handling emergencies only.

On Saturday, the official ZIANA news agency reported that the situation at hopsitals was critical, with one hospital on the outskirts of the capital Harare forced to close seven wards while some patients were dying because they lacked medical care.
It quoted some doctors at Harare Central, Harare's biggest hospital, as saying they had to postpone surgical operations because there were no nurses in the theatre.
